objective:
Build the question corpus, its record-and-replay scoring and regression gate (same idea as the tag corpus, ADR-033), an on-phone recorder in the debug "AI test set" screen, an import script, and fix one known how-often edge case in Explore. The orchestrator will record on the Pixel 10 Pro afterwards and write the baseline by hand; you do NOT touch a device and do NOT create question-baseline.json or question-device-latest.json.

Read first: docs/SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md section 12 (tag corpus, TG1.4 replay/report/gate, TG1.4a in-app runner) and the existing tag-corpus code it names in core-testing (TagCorpusModel.kt, TagCorpus.kt, TagRecording.kt, TagReplay.kt, TagReport.kt, TagGate.kt and their tests incl. TagRecordingFilesTest, TagRegressionGateTest), scripts/semantic/import-tag-recording.sh, app-phone src/debug (TagCorpusRun, TagCorpusRunnerActivity, TagCorpusRunnerScreen, AndroidManifest.xml, res/xml/debugtools_file_paths.xml, res/values/debugtools_strings.xml) and src/testDebug tests; core-domain lookup/LookupService.kt (QuestionCandidate, QuestionExtractor, LookupOutcome, LookupService.ask(text, today, firstDayOfWeek)), QuestionKind.kt, QuestionKindDetector.kt, QuestionScope.kt, HistoryLookup.kt (LookupEntry, LookupTarget, rank), repository/TagRepository.kt, tagging/TagCatalog types; temporal/TemporalRangeResolver.kt; stats/DateRange.kt (DateRangeSelection); core-ai GeminiNanoQuestionExtractor.kt, QuestionPrompt.kt, QuestionResponse.kt and core-ai test QuestionPromptTest.kt; app-phone ui/explore/ExploreViewModel.kt (howOften, entriesAllTime, recompute, PendingQuestion) and its tests.

PART A -- question corpus (core-testing, package ...core.testing.corpus, new files prefixed Question*):
1. `core-testing/src/main/resources/semantic-corpus/question-corpus.json` (UTF-8, LF only), loaded by `QuestionCorpus.load()` / `parse(bytes)` / `case(id)` / `sha256` (SHA-256 of the file bytes) like TagCorpus. Strict decoding exactly like the tag corpus (unknown keys rejected, every field without a default required, incl. nullable ones). Shape `{ schemaVersion: 1, description, catalogs, cases }`.
2. Catalog fixtures (`catalogs`): each has `subjects` and `actions` (`{ id, displayName, aliases }`, ids `subj-`/`act-`) and `entries` (`{ id, subjectId, actionId, occurredAt }`, ISO offset date-time; these become LookupEntry rows; durationSeconds null). Two fixtures: `empty` (no tags, no entries) and `household-q`: a synthetic household of about 8 subjects and 8 actions with aliases, entries spread over 2025-06 .. 2026-10-05, including: lawn (alias yard) + mow: exactly 4 entries in August 2026 and some in Jun/Jul/Sep 2026; car (alias truck) + change oil: >= 4 entries roughly every 4 months; furnace + change filter: a few, the last one in September 2026; hot tub + add chlorine: many; dogs + walk: many incl. last week; something with exactly 2 entries all time (for the 'not enough entries to say how often' case); an action shared by two subjects (e.g. clean: gutters is NOT a subject -- the gutters must not exist anywhere -- but e.g. grill + clean and windows + clean). Nothing logged after 2026-10-05. No real captures or owner data: everything synthetic.
3. Case fields: `id`, `group` (one of LAST_TIME, COUNT, HOW_OFTEN, LIST, DATE_ONLY, NOT_LOGGED, TRICKY), `catalog`, `question`, `today` (all "2026-10-05"), `zoneId` (all "America/Detroit"), `firstDayOfWeek` (all "SUNDAY"), `expected`, optional `note`. `expected` = { `outcome`: ANSWER | BROWSE | NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY; `subjectIds`: acceptable resolved subject tag ids for ANSWER (empty list = subject must be unset); `actionIds`: same for the action; `mustNotMatch`: tag ids that must never be in the target; `kind`: expected QuestionKind; `allowedKinds`: extra acceptable kinds (may be empty); `range`: either {"preset": "ALL_TIME"} or {"from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "to": "YYYY-MM-DD"} (inclusive local dates of the resolved DateRangeSelection; compare dates only, not labels); `dateWords`: NONE | USED | NOT_UNDERSTOOD }. For NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY, subjectIds/actionIds empty and kind/range/dateWords are still given but not scored.
4. About 40 cases, all synthetic. Must include: "How many times did I mow the lawn in August?" (COUNT, lawn+mow, 2026-08-01..2026-08-31, USED); "How often do I change the oil?" (HOW_OFTEN, car+change oil, ALL_TIME, NONE); "When was the last time I cleaned the gutters?" (NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY: gutters never logged; must not answer with grill/windows clean); "When did I last change the furnace filter?"; "What did I do last week?" (BROWSE, previous calendar week Sun 2026-09-27..Sat 2026-10-03, LIST); a yard alias question; a question naming only an action; a question naming only a subject; counts with 'this year', 'last month', 'in 2025', 'since June', 'in the past 30 days', 'yesterday'; a future window ("next week") -> NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY; date words no rule understands (e.g. "around the holidays") -> ANSWER with ALL_TIME + NOT_UNDERSTOOD; 'Did I ever ...' and 'Have I ever ...'; questions without a trailing '?' that QuestionDetector still accepts; at least 3 against the `empty` catalog (all NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY). Expected values are what the product SHOULD do (program logic decides kind first from text rules, then the model; work out each case's expectation from QuestionKindDetector, TemporalRangeResolver and TagResolver rules, and the obvious correct tag), never what a model happens to answer. None of the five worked-example questions in core-ai QuestionPrompt.kt may appear, and none of their subjects (gutters is allowed only as the NOT_LOGGED case phrased differently from the prompt's example -- the prompt has "When did I last clean the gutters?"; keep the corpus wording different as above).
5. Tests: `QuestionCorpusIntegrityTest` (decodes strictly; ids unique; every catalog reference and expected tag id exists in its fixture; entries reference existing tags; no entry after the case's today; LF only; group counts pinned; the required cases above present verbatim; every question passes QuestionDetector.isQuestion); `QuestionCorpusOracleTest`: feed a hand-written IDEAL candidate per case (subject/action/dateWindow/kind words a perfect reader would return; keep them in the test) through the real LookupService and assert every case scores CORRECT with the scorer from PART B (proves expectations and deterministic logic agree; list any unavoidable gap in a KNOWN_GAPS set asserted to be exactly the failing set -- it should be empty). Extend core-ai `QuestionPromptTest`'s 'no corpus sentence appears in the prompt' test to include QuestionCorpus questions.

PART B -- recording, replay, report, gate (core-testing):
6. `QuestionRecording.kt`: formatVersion 1, strict like TagRecording. Header: source (RecordingSource), modelLabel, deviceModel, interpreterVersion, promptVersion, schemaVersion, questionCorpusSha256, recordedAt, notes; entries: caseId, `answer` (subject, action, dateWindow: String?, kind: QuestionKind) XOR failureKind, latencyMs. `QuestionRecordingEntry.of(caseId, QuestionExtractionResult, latencyMs)`. No question text and no raw model text in the format.
7. `QuestionReplay.kt`: rejects stale recordings (hash differs or not exactly one entry per case) with the existing StaleRecordingException. For each answered entry, runs the REAL `LookupService(repository, extractor)` (default TemporalRangeResolver) with a replaying QuestionExtractor returning the recorded candidate and a read-only TagRepository built from the case's fixture (loadTagCatalog + loadLookupEntries; every other method throws UnsupportedOperationException), with `ask(case.question, LocalDate.parse(case.today), DayOfWeek.valueOf(case.firstDayOfWeek))`. Classes (`QuestionReplayClass`), exactly one per case:
   - WRONG: expected NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY but got ANSWER or BROWSE; or ANSWER/BROWSE where the other was expected; or ANSWER with a target subject/action id not in subjectIds/actionIds (a side that must be unset but is set, or vice versa, counts) or in mustNotMatch; or a resolved range whose dates differ from the expected one while dateWords == USED (the user is shown wrong dates without warning); or a kind outside kind+allowedKinds when it changes the answer line (treat any kind mismatch as WRONG; keep it simple).
   - SAFE_MISS: ANSWER/BROWSE expected but NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY returned; or the range fell back to ALL_TIME with dateWords NOT_UNDERSTOOD when a USED range was expected (the user is told the dates were not understood); or ALL_TIME with NONE when USED was expected (the model dropped the date words: shown as All time on the chip, which the user can see) -- record a reason code for each (NOTHING_FOUND, DATES_NOT_UNDERSTOOD, DATES_DROPPED).
   - CORRECT: outcome, target ids, kind, range dates and dateWords all as expected (dateWords must match exactly for CORRECT).
   - FAILED: the extractor gave no answer (any failureKind).
   Reason codes enum `QuestionCheck` for WRONG too (UNEXPECTED_ANSWER, WRONG_OUTCOME, WRONG_SUBJECT, WRONG_ACTION, MUST_NOT_MATCH, WRONG_RANGE, WRONG_KIND). Result per entry holds case id, group, class, codes, the outcome type, resolved ids, kind, range dates and dateWords -- NEVER the recorded model words (the report must not be able to show them; prove it with a sentinel test like TagReportTest).
8. `QuestionReport.kt`: Markdown at `core-testing/build/reports/semantic-corpus/question-device.md` (stand-in recordings are out of scope; only DEVICE is supported -- reject other sources with a clear error): provenance, totals per class, per-group table, then one row per non-CORRECT case: id, group, class, codes, what it resolved to (ids, kind, range, dateWords), the expected values and the committed corpus question. Console summary: ids, counts and codes only.
9. `QuestionGate.kt`: baseline `core-testing/src/test/resources/semantic-corpus/recordings/question-baseline.json` = `{ "mustStayCorrect": [...], "maxWrong": N }` (every key required, unknown keys rejected, ids unique, maxWrong >= 0). Fails when a mustStayCorrect case is not CORRECT, WRONG count > maxWrong, or a baseline id is not in the corpus.
10. Tests: QuestionRecordingTest (round trip, strictness, answer XOR failure), QuestionReplayScorerTest (every class and code with small synthetic recordings), QuestionReportTest (sentinel: recorded words never appear), QuestionGateTest, and `QuestionRecordingFilesTest` + `QuestionRegressionGateTest` mirroring TagRecordingFilesTest / TagRegressionGateTest for `recordings/question-device-latest.json`: absent recording -> skip (JUnit assumption); present -> structural check / replay, write the report, then gate only if question-baseline.json exists (absent baseline -> report written, gate skipped); malformed or stale -> fail.

PART C -- on-phone recorder (app-phone debug only) and import script:
11. `debugtools/QuestionCorpusRun.kt`: same contract as TagCorpusRun (every case once in corpus order, extractor input is ONLY the question text, same FAST_REFUSAL_MS / THROTTLE_KINDS / BUSY_BACKOFF_MS backoff -- reuse TagCorpusRun's companion constants rather than copying them, cancellation propagates, numbers only, injected clocks) producing a QuestionRecording (source DEVICE, modelLabel = TagCorpusRun.MODEL_LABEL, questionCorpusSha256, notes "in-app runner; busy retries: N") and a numbers-only result.
12. The existing "AI test set" activity/screen gains a second set: a "Run question set" button next to the existing Run (the existing button may be relabelled "Run logging set"), sharing the same readiness gate, foreground/keep-screen-on/cancel-on-stop rules and progress/summary display. The question run uses the real `GeminiNanoQuestionExtractor` exactly as the app constructs it (check how app-phone builds it; wrapping in BusyRetryQuestionExtractor is NOT wanted -- the runner has its own backoff, like the tag run). Output written atomically to `<filesDir>/question-corpus/question-device-recording.json`; add `<files-path name="question_corpus" path="question-corpus/" />` to debugtools_file_paths.xml; a Share button for the question file like the tag one. Only one run at a time. Strings in debugtools_strings.xml. Update the manifest/xml comments accordingly. Nothing in the release build.
13. Tests in src/testDebug: QuestionCorpusRunTest (order, one call per case, input is the question text, backoff, cancellation, provenance/hash), and extend TagCorpusRunnerScreenTest for the two buttons/states.
14. `scripts/semantic/import-question-recording.sh`, mirroring import-tag-recording.sh: stage into build/question-recording-import/, cheap check (parses, source DEVICE, formatVersion 1, has entries), backup + overwrite `core-testing/src/test/resources/semantic-corpus/recordings/question-device-latest.json`, then run QuestionRecordingFilesTest and QuestionRegressionGateTest; same exit codes (0 / 1 / 3). Make it executable (git update-index --chmod=+x is NOT yours; just create the file with a #!/usr/bin/env bash shebang).

PART D -- Explore how-often edge case (app-phone ui/explore):
15. Known bug: a HOW_OFTEN question with date words (e.g. "How often did I walk the dogs in July?") takes the gap and the all-time count from the summary of the date-filtered view, whose activity rows only include activities with entries in that window; when nothing was logged in the window it says "not enough entries yet to say how often (0 so far)" even when older entries exist. Fix: for a HOW_OFTEN answer, compute the gap, entriesAllTime, activityCount and lastTime from an ExploreCalculator summary of the SAME tags with range ALL_TIME (the typical gap is an all-time measure by the counting rules), while the chips and the rest of the screen keep the question's date range. Keep the existing stale-result guard. Update the howOften KDoc. Tests: HOW_OFTEN + date window with zero entries in the window but >=3 older entries -> gap present and the all-time count; HOW_OFTEN + window with entries -> same gap as without the window; existing tests keep passing.

Rules: model output is untrusted and only ever passes through the real LookupService (tag resolution + TemporalRangeResolver); the model never produces a date, count or answer (ADR-011/051/052); no question text, corpus text or model output in logs or console (recorders and tests print ids, counts, codes, timings only; AGENTS.md #11); the capture corpus (corpus.json, tag-corpus.json, their recordings and baselines) must not change; core-ai main code, the question prompt and its version must not change; nothing in the release build gains corpus code; the debug runner never downloads the model (ADR-031).
non_goals: No device work: do not run adb, install anything, or create question-device-latest.json or question-baseline.json (orchestrator).
No stand-in (Ollama) question recorder and no instrumented androidTest question recorder.
No change to core-ai main code, the question prompt (q2) or its version, the capture/tag corpora, their recordings or baselines.
No change to core-domain main code (LookupService, QuestionKindDetector, TemporalRangeResolver, TagResolver, stats).
acceptance_criteria: question-corpus.json exists with the fixtures, fields and ~40 synthetic cases described, including every required case verbatim; QuestionCorpus loads it strictly with a SHA-256; integrity test pins structure and group counts.
QuestionCorpusOracleTest passes every case CORRECT through the real LookupService with ideal candidates (KNOWN_GAPS empty or exactly the failing set, each justified).

QuestionRecording / QuestionReplay / QuestionReport / QuestionGate implement the format, stale-rejection, classes and codes, report and gate as specified; replay uses the real LookupService and default TemporalRangeResolver, never a copy; no recorded model words reach the replay result or report (sentinel test).
QuestionRecordingFilesTest and QuestionRegressionGateTest skip cleanly with no recording, write the report when a recording exists, and gate only when question-baseline.json exists.

The debug AI test set screen can run the question set through the real GeminiNanoQuestionExtractor with the same readiness, foreground, backoff, numbers-only and atomic-write rules as the tag run, writing files/question-corpus/question-device-recording.json and sharing it; nothing added to the release build.
import-question-recording.sh mirrors import-tag-recording.sh for the question recording.
Explore HOW_OFTEN answers take gap, all-time count, activity count and last time from an all-time summary of the same tags, with tests for the zero-entries-in-window case.
QuestionPromptTest asserts no question-corpus question appears in the prompt.
No question, corpus text or model output is logged or printed.
No file outside write_paths is changed.
